piezas.titulo: Reading words: Name, country and introductions
texto: Reading and spelling of pronouns and countries: «ชื่อ» has the initial consonant ช (low class), the upper closed vowel ื and the tone mark ่ (mái eek), which, with low-class consonants, gives a falling tone. The word «ประเทศ» (pràthêet, country) has an initial consonant cluster ปร and ends in ศ, which at the end of a syllable sounds like the voiceless alveolar stop [t] (rule แม่กด). Recognising these rules helps you decode passports, customs forms and business cards.

pregunta.texto: In the word «ประเทศ» (country), how is the final consonant ศ pronounced?

opciones.texto: As a voiceless stop [t] (แม่กด group)
opciones.explicacion: Correct: at the end of a syllable, sibilants such as ศ, ษ, ส are neutralised to the sound [t].
Incorrect: standard Thai does not allow [s] fricatives as syllable endings.
Incorrect: ศ is a consonant, not a vowel sign.
